events.text: The Prophet ﷺ is orphaned of his mother Aminah

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ lost his mother at about six years of age, some thirty-four years before revelation began.

events.text: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib accepts Islam

easy.explain: Hamza accepted Islam during the Makkan years and was killed at Uhud, about nine years later.

events.text: Bilal ibn Rabah is persecuted in Makkah
Bilal gives the adhan at the conquest of Makkah

easy.explain: Bilal was tortured for his faith in Makkah and later called the adhan from atop the Ka'bah when the city was taken.

events.text: The Muslims are commanded to face Jerusalem in prayer
The qiblah is changed to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: Jerusalem was the first qiblah; the direction was changed to the Ka'bah in the second year after the Hijrah.

events.text: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib leads the migrants in Abyssinia

easy.explain: Ja'far spoke for the Muslims before the Negus in Abyssinia and was killed years later at Mu'tah.

events.text: Salman al-Farisi suggests digging a trench

easy.explain: Salman's suggestion shaped the defence of Madinah at Khandaq, three years before Makkah was entered.

events.text: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to teach in Yathrib

easy.explain: Mus'ab was sent to Yathrib after the first Pledge of Aqabah and was killed at Uhud a few years later.
Abu Bakr was among the first to believe and became the first caliph some twenty-two years later.

events.text: Khalid ibn al-Walid fights against the Muslims at Uhud
Khalid commands Muslim forces at Yarmuk

easy.explain: Khalid fought against the Muslims at Uhud, accepted Islam before the conquest of Makkah, and later commanded at Yarmuk.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ is placed in the care of his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib
The Prophet ﷺ is placed in the care of his uncle Abu Talib

easy.explain: After his mother's death the Prophet ﷺ was cared for by his grandfather, and on his death about two years later by his uncle Abu Talib.

medium.explain: Hamza, called the chief of the martyrs, accepted Islam in Makkah and was killed at Uhud five years before the city was taken.

events.text: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to Yathrib

medium.explain: Mus'ab's teaching in Yathrib prepared the ground for the second pledge and the migration that followed.
Khalid accepted Islam shortly before Mu'tah, where he took command after three leaders fell, and later commanded at Yarmuk.

events.text: Ja'far ibn Abi Talib migrates to Abyssinia
Ja'far returns at the time of Khaybar

medium.explain: Ja'far led the migrants in Abyssinia for years, returned around the time of Khaybar, and was killed at Mu'tah the following year.

events.text: Bilal gives the adhan at the conquest of Makkah

medium.explain: Bilal endured torture in Makkah, called the adhan at its conquest, and settled in Syria after the Prophet's passing.
Abu Bakr was among the first to believe, the Prophet's companion in the cave during the Hijrah, and the first caliph.
Umar accepted Islam in Makkah, became the second caliph, and travelled to Jerusalem to receive the city's surrender.

events.text: The trench is dug at Khandaq
Salman is appointed governor of Mada'in

medium.explain: Salman, originally from Persia, suggested the trench that defended Madinah, and later served as a governor under Umar.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ loses his mother
The Prophet ﷺ loses his grandfather
The Prophet ﷺ loses his uncle Abu Talib

medium.explain: Three successive losses of those who cared for him, the last in the Year of Sorrow.

events.text: Zayd ibn Harithah is freed and adopted

medium.explain: Zayd ibn Harithah was among the first to accept Islam and was killed leading at Mu'tah, where he was the first of three commanders to fall.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ loses his mother Aminah
He loses his grandfather Abd al-Muttalib
He travels to Syria with Abu Talib

hard.explain: The years before the mission, from early bereavement through the journey to Syria and marriage, to the rebuilding of the Ka'bah.
Conversions spanning the whole mission, from the earliest believers in Makkah to the leaders of the Quraysh at the conquest.

events.text: Mus'ab ibn Umayr is sent to Yathrib
Mus'ab carries the banner at Badr

hard.explain: The life of Mus'ab ibn Umayr from his mission to Yathrib to his death at Uhud.

events.text: Ja'far returns at the time of Khaybar
Zayd and Ja'far are killed at Mu'tah
Khalid withdraws the army from Mu'tah

hard.explain: The threads leading to Mu'tah, where Zayd, Ja'far and Abdullah ibn Rawahah fell in succession before Khalid took command.

events.text: Bilal gives the adhan at the conquest of Makkah

hard.explain: The life of Bilal ibn Rabah, from persecution in Makkah to calling the adhan over the conquered city.
The arc of Umar's life from his acceptance of Islam in Makkah to his assassination in Madinah.

events.text: Khalid fights against the Muslims at Uhud
Khalid fights in the Ridda campaigns

hard.explain: Khalid ibn al-Walid's path from opposing the Muslims at Uhud to commanding at Yarmuk.

events.text: Zayd ibn Thabit serves as a scribe of revelation
Zayd compiles the Qur'an under Abu Bakr
Zayd leads the standardisation under Uthman

hard.explain: Zayd ibn Thabit's role in the preservation of the Qur'an, from scribe to the two great compilations.

events.text: Aisha is present at the Battle of the Camel

hard.explain: Aisha's life after the Hijrah. Surah An-Nur was revealed in connection with the slander against her, and she became one of the foremost narrators of hadith.
The two grandsons of the Prophet ﷺ, from their births in Madinah to Karbala.

events.text: Abu Hurayrah serves as governor of Bahrain

hard.explain: Abu Hurayrah accepted Islam around the time of Khaybar and, in a few years of companionship, became the most prolific narrator of hadith.

events.text: Uthman is sent as envoy to Makkah at Hudaybiyyah

hard.explain: Uthman ibn Affan's life. The rumour of his death as envoy at Hudaybiyyah prompted the Pledge of Ridwan.

events.text: The trench is dug at Khandaq
Salman serves as governor of Mada'in

hard.explain: Salman al-Farisi, originally from Persia, whose suggestion of the trench shaped the defence of Madinah.
